topics.label: Introduction and Lecture Overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture on the initiation and resolution of inflammation and outlines how familiar immune components will be integrated.

topics.label: Innate Recognition of Pathogens and Cellular Damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular mechanisms by which the innate immune system senses microbial infections and tissue injury through PAMPs, DAMPs, pattern recognition receptors, and downstream signaling complexes.

topics.label: Cellular Dynamics and Physiological Consequences of Inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how activated immune and endothelial cells coordinate leukocyte recruitment and trafficking, as well as the systemic physiological consequences of severe inflammatory activation.

topics.label: Resolution of Inflammation, Tissue Repair, and Chronic Pathology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how acute inflammation is resolved, how damaged tissue undergoes repair, and how persistent stimuli lead to chronic inflammation and granuloma formation.

topics.label: Conclusion and Next Lecture Preview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture and previews the upcoming session on the complement system.
